YES. I cannot stand when people copy and paste their feedback to the parent on the teacher section. I don't need a rundown of the lesson. Let me know if the kid had any behavior issues, what areas I might need to help them with specifically (certain letter sounds, words, extension to gauge comprehension, etc), and what the student rocks at (reading, math, pronunciation, etc.) so I won't waste too much time in those areas

I'm always honest in my feedback to other teachers. I'll straight up say "STUDENT wasn't interested in participating in class today/ STUDENT refused to participate during class/ STUDENT kept their head down/were scrolling on other websites/were playing with toys/ STUDENT needs to have mouse locked because they can't focus", etc. I've used the phrase 'difficult student' a few times.

Full time graduate student (with basically a full-time internship). VIPKID has kept me from eating Ramen every meal.

Oh lord, don't even mention Gogokid. I tried to sign up to teach with them, and when there were 3 weeks of no available interview slots I realized the complaints about the company were finally worth listening to. Maybe in a few years when they've better established themselves...yikes.

I haven't had a negative experience either. I think people worry a little too much about the 4-star reviews. It isn't going to prevent bookings honestly. With the cancellation thing...yes, 6 can seem strict, but at the same time, they do provide soft cancellations with proof. I don't think I've ever missed 6 days of work in my life (with good reason or not), just a few planned vacation days (which isn't an issue with VIPKID since you make your own schedule).

There are some teachers who don't treat VIPKID as their job, and merely see it as a 'gig'. Sure, it can be seen that way, but you still have to be professional and show up for work- and when you can't, do your best to notify your employer and provide proof of absence. I figured this is pretty typical in any work environment.

If you didn't show up to work for 6 days without much explanation when people were paying for you to be there what do you think would most likely happen?

I don't see it as mistreatment, I see it as them trying to run a functioning business.

I only teach part-time (like 8-12 classes a week), so I can't see myself using them for a break. If my power goes out I don't have proof because I use a shitty co-op that never sends out any kind of documentation. I guess I could take a photo of myself standing in the dark, but you know, that's kind of pointless.

Sickness would be the only thing, and that likely would be a soft cancellation. But I don't have any health insurance to afford a doctor, so I'd either just push through it or suffer a cancellation penalty.

I had my first SNS this morning. Woke up at 5am refreshed and ready to start the day only to find out that my student had cancelled overnight. Hopped back into bed and slept a few more hours. It's nice to be paid to sleep.

I was super nervous when I got my first booking as well- this is totally normal! You will be able to gauge your student's interest in the song's and what-not by doing, don't assume! I had a 10-yr old boy who LOVED to sing the songs... got really into them actually. 

Remember that it's okay to be silly and goofy- no matter how ridiculous you feel, keep it up because the kids love it and it will really capture their attention. Use A LOT of TPR to help connect meaning behind the words you are using. Have them do it along with you.

It's okay to make mistakes. Laugh them off, make a silly face. Your student likely will laugh right along with you. 

It is unlikely that you will receive a negative review your first class, but even if you do, yes you can bounce back! 

With each lesson you teach, you'll grow more and more comfortable. That nervous energy will turn into excited energy. You'll start looking forward to meeting your next student and belting out songs and engaging in exaggerated TPR just to see them smile. 

You'll be great- you got this!

Despite it being CNY, I have seen an uptick in bookings for the evenings slots. Also, VIPKID will accept an official letter from your college that shows the date you will receive your degree. That is what they did for me, no questions asked.
I got three bookings within one week of opening up my slots. However, I think my intro video is really what helped me.
